newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee called to open 3.00 cents lower.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee called to open 3.00 cents lower.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures were called to open down 3.00 cents Thursday in a technical correction to Wednesday's sharp run-up, traders said.
New York arabica futures surged yesterday, with five contracts setting new life-of-contract highs, as continued supply woes fueled speculative buying.

Active July jumped 11.45 cents to end at 210.40 cents a lb after ranging between a new lifetime high of 212.00 and 200.40 cents. Spot May soared 12.65 cents to 239.05 cents, while the back months closed 4.00 to 8.55 higher.
The May/July switch, a barometer of nearby availability, widened to 28.65 today from 27.45 at the close on Tuesday.

After Wednesday's close, CSCE reported certified coffee inventories increased for the first time since March 31. Stocks rose 565 bags to 47,668 bags as of April 29. There were 2,000 bags of coffee pending grading, the exchange said.
LIFFE coffee futures were broadly higher midday Thursday, but origin selling cut into early gains. At the break, July was up $42, to $1,660, after peaking at $1,690.
